note: Held out. See README.md in this directory for why, and for the harness assertion that keeps it held out.

derivation.why: Revision D section 3 reduces the hydrocarbon minimum to 8.0 mm, and section 3.1 suspends that reduction for any course recording pitting until a pitting assessment is accepted. The inspection report records external pitting adjacent to point C on the course being assessed, and no pitting assessment exists in the corpus. The Revision C value of 9.0 mm therefore governs.
derivation.trap: An answer that cites Revision D's headline 8.0 mm concludes 8.2 mm is acceptable. It is the newest revision and it is the wrong answer, which is what makes this a conflict test rather than a recency test.

cases.working: 0.354 in x 25.4 mm/in = 8.9916 mm. (8.9916 - 8.2) / 8.9916 * 100 = 8.8038. The 0.01 band covers rounding the conversion, not a different basis.
cases.wrong_answer_to_reject: Any answer derived from (0.354 - 8.2), which is negative and enormous as a percentage.

must_state: 31.7% is loss against the 12.0 mm nominal thickness
the SOP defines wall loss against the minimum allowable thickness
the SOP figure is 8.9% (to one decimal place)
cases.note: The claimed arithmetic is correct: (12.0-8.2)/12.0*100 = 31.67. Verifying the arithmetic and stopping there is the failure this case detects.

cases.wrong_answer_to_reject: 2026-11-12, which is three calendar months rather than 90 days.

cases.working: 2024-03-18 to 2026-08-12 is 877 days. 1.4 mm lost. At 365.25 d/yr: 1.4 / (877/365.25) = 0.58307. At 365 d/yr: 0.58267. The band covers both conventions and nothing wider.
cases.wrong_answer_to_reject: 0.70 mm/yr, which is 1.4 mm divided by 2 whole years.

must_state: a minimum allowable thickness of zero gives no percentage

cases.note: Read from the scanned page, not from the Markdown source.
External pitting adjacent to point C. This is the fact that engages Revision D section 3.1, so an extraction that misses it produces a wrong assessment downstream.
The report states internal inspection was not performed. An agent that describes internal surface condition as observed has fabricated it.

must_state: Revision D section 3.1 is engaged because pitting is recorded
two revisions of the SOP are in the corpus
they give different minimum allowable thicknesses for hydrocarbon service
which one governs this assessment, and why
